claim_under_attack.claim_text: Every repair id in the portfolio maps to exactly one repair, and every done_check glob matches only its own item's receipts.

qualitative_notes.R-A11: Two independently-conceived defects, both 'anchored signature-identity re-issue' repairs, coincidentally assigned the same auto-incremented Wave-R id: amphora-design-rule-score/R-A11 re-issues guth-gold-physical-baseline-v1/physical_baseline_receipt.v1.json; amphora-molecule-property/R-A11 re-issues phys-ml-stack-comparison-c8-fire2-clean-subset-v1/c8_fire2_dielectric_clean_subset_receipt.v1.json. Different target artifacts, different module field in payload, different file sha256. This is a true ID-ASSIGNMENT COLLISION (unrelated repairs, same id) -- already flagged non-fatal by R-Z99 (2026-08-05) but left unresolved.
qualitative_notes.R-A12: Signing-key-selection-bug reinstatement batch, rolled out per-module under the SAME id by design (root_cause identical string in both payloads: 'Signing-key selection bug in the hourly cron fires...'). amphora-molecule-role-ranker/R-A12 and amphora-sourceability-ehs/R-A12 share a filename (ra12_reinstatement_batch_receipt.v1.dsse.json) but differ in file sha256 and in payload module_id/reinstated_artifacts -- this is INTENTIONAL id reuse for one conceptual multi-module batch fix, not an accidental collision, but it is still an id shared across module namespaces with no schema field disambiguating batch-siblings from coincidental collisions.
qualitative_notes.R-N02: Coordinated C=N amine-exclusion fix, independently re-implemented and verified in 3 modules under the same id (amphora-molecule-property, amphora-molecule-role-ranker, amphora-rdkit-ffi), each with its own V-N02a/b/c independent-verify campaign item. Distinct filenames, distinct file sha256 per module. Same pattern as R-A12: deliberate coordinated reuse, not a coincidental collision.

reachability_simulation.method: Reproduced lib/remote_verify.py mode=donecheck exactly: glob.glob(os.path.join(root, pat), recursive=True) where root is the single shared mvp20-split checkout and pat is the item's done_check.glob string. For every collision, built the glob string AS IF owned by each colliding module in turn and checked whether any match falls outside that module's own subtree.

recommended_fix: (a) Add a namespace-collision linter (outside lib/remote_verify.py, which is baseline-hashed) that fails CI/campaign-authoring if a new repair id's directory already exists under a DIFFERENT module with a different root_cause/action fingerprint; (b) require every batch repair item's payload to carry an explicit 'batch_sibling_of' array so intentional cross-module id reuse (R-A12, R-N02 pattern) is schema-distinguishable from accidental collision (R-A11 pattern) instead of requiring a manual audit like this one to tell them apart.
verdict_reasoning: CLAIM has two conjuncts. (1) id-uniqueness: REFUTED by direct enumeration -- 3 ids (R-A11, R-A12, R-N02) are each used by more than one module's repair item, across 7 total repair instances. This alone falsifies 'every repair id maps to exactly one repair.' (2) done_check-glob false-done reachability: investigated exhaustively via source-level reproduction of the ONLY mechanism that currently evaluates done_check (lib/remote_verify.py mode=donecheck) against the ONLY glob strings that currently exist for structured items (100% of the 111 live campaign.json done_check.glob entries, 0/111 lacking their own module-name prefix). Under that mechanism, os.path.join(root, pat) with pat always starting '<owning-module>/' makes cross-module matches structurally impossible regardless of trailing <id> collisions -- confirmed empirically for all 3 colliding ids: 0/7 reachability tests show a match outside the intended module. No byte-identical receipt is filed under two different modules' done/ dirs (R-A12's identically-NAMED file differs in content); no unsigned or cross-module DSSE was found. This part of the claim therefore SURVIVES the strongest available attack against the current enforcement mechanism. Residual gap: the ORIGINAL done_check definitions used when the R-A11/R-A12/R-N02 items were themselves marked done are not recoverable (they predate this repo's git history and are no longer present in campaign.json), so historical reachability at time-of-completion cannot be verified either way -- reported as an open, non-fabricated gap, not assumed safe.
